beats.lead: You've seen this quoted a thousand times.
beats.text: "There are only two hard things in Computer Science: cache invalidation and naming things."
beats.note: It's credited to one man, Phil Karlton, and nobody has ever produced anything he wrote it in.

beats.lead: His own son went looking for the source.
beats.note: In a 2017 post, David Karlton collected every citation of the quote he could find online and admitted none of them traced back further than secondhand memory.

beats.name: Phil Karlton
beats.role: Engineer at Xerox PARC, DEC, Silicon Graphics and Netscape, where he helped build X Windows and an internet security protocol. Killed in a car accident near Canelli, Italy, that June, at 50, taking the actual origin of his own line with him.

beats.lead: One colleague's memory reaches further back than the Netscape story most people repeat.
beats.text: He recalls hearing it at Carnegie Mellon, around 1970.
beats.note: Karlton really did study there, years before his Xerox and Netscape career, but the memory is one blog comment, not a document, so the earliest confirmed instance of his own line is still unknown.

beats.text: The internet gave it a third hard thing anyway: off-by-one errors.

beats.line: A quote everyone can cite and nobody can source.
